intro: Correlated columns make coordinates harder to interpret. Subtract earlier directions one by one to build an orthonormal basis and triangular coordinates.
task: Implement modified Gram–Schmidt and return thin Q and upper-triangular R with positive diagonal.
requirements: matrix has shape (n,k) with n>=k. Every residual column norm encountered in order must exceed 1e-10.
For each column, subtract its projections on already normalized columns in sequence, store those coefficients in R, then normalize the residual.
Return {"q": Q, "r": R} with Q shape (n,k) and R shape (k,k). Reject numerically dependent columns; do not silently drop them.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Upper triangular input
Scaled axes
Negative column orientation

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: The next basis vector is the portion of a column unexplained by all earlier basis vectors.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Update the residual after each projection, and store that coefficient before normalizing the remaining direction.

explanation: Each new column splits into components along existing basis vectors and an orthogonal residual. The projection coefficients form R, while normalized residuals form Q.
Modified Gram–Schmidt updates the residual after every subtraction. Its positive normalization denominator fixes the otherwise arbitrary sign of each basis column.
